items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: He played at the Belmont for Mr. Brown.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, then they split it up with the band.

Now, how that happened was that a fellow called Freddy Tunstall. Tomsill. He played at the Belmont for Mr. Brown. And he got mad one night, one Sunday night, and left. And Brown knew that I was around there and wasn't working at the time. So he said send somebody and tell them to send for me and I'd come there. He said, "Son, how would you like to go upstairs and play for me?" Cause, he said, "you see, I'm stuck. Freddy's gone back to New York and left me." I told him that, "Mr. Brown, you know I can't play for…

drum. You just had to beat it out and play enough for the dancing. But, I could do that, because I had all that training at playing for house parties. And I handled that I could kind of swing good, then, you see?
